newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rheinmetall 1996 profits, sales, orders up.
newsitem.headline: Rheinmetall 1996 profits, sales, orders up.

text.p: German defence and engineering group Rheinmetall AG said on Thursday it had "significantly increased" profits in 1996 as both sales and orders gained ground.
Group sales last year climbed 10.2 percent to 3.66 billion marks ($2.2 billion), while orders jumped 23.1 percent to 4.46 billion marks.
Rheinmetall said recent acquisitions would help it double sales this year to around seven billion marks and boost profits towards 100 million marks.
Rheinmetall said in a letter to shareholders it had shaken off the earnings weakness from the 1992-95 recession.
"Net profits at the listed holding company Rheinmetall AG will be higher than in the previous year, continuing the positive development of previous years," the company said.
Group net profit in 1995 was 2.6 million marks, while parent net was 6.4 million marks.

The company said 1997 had begun successfully. It added the acquisitions of the Hirschmann and STN Atlas electronics firms and purchase of shares in autoparts firm Kolbenschmidt would put Rheinmetall "into a new league".
The STN Atlas takeover awaits regulatory approval.
Rheinmetall also said its strategy had been welcomed by the stock market, with both its ordinary and preferred shares rising by over 50 percent since November.
Rheinmetall ordinaries, listed on Frankfurt's MDAX mid-cap market, were unchanged at 295 marks at mid-session on Thursday, while preferreds were down three at 239 marks.

The company said it was reorganising its business into five key areas, with three core engineering divisions -- defence, automotive and machinebuilding -- and two electronics sectors -- industry and defence.

Hirschmann will, together with Preh and other civil operations, be fused into Rheinmetall's industrial electronics division. STN Atlas, once Brussels grants takeover approval, will form the defence electronics group.
Both sectors are expected to turn profits this year.

Uncertainty over Germany's defence budget will require more restructuring in the Rheinmetall Industrie AG military engineering operation. The group will continue to seek foreign partners, but still expects to turn a profit this year.

The Jagenberg AG machinebuilding division will launch an innovation offensive to consolidate its turnaround, and is expected to post a higher profit in line with the pre-recession years, helped by the weaker German mark, Rheinmetall said.
Automotive supplier Pierburg AG will launch new product lines and seek to counter price pressure from German car makers in order to post an acceptable earnings result.
For the year just ended, Jagenbau increased profits by 60 million marks, stripping out extraordinary items, to achieve a "significantly positive net result", Rheinmetall said.
Pierburg managed through product development, a big rise in turnover and tight cost control to secure a positive result.

Rheinmetall Industrie managed, despite defence budget cuts, "to make an appropriate contribution" to 1996 results. The group's small Mauser Waldeck AG office furniture business made a loss due to restructuring charges.

At the end of 1996, the Rheinmetall group employed 14,300 workers, down 1.7 percent, and personnel costs rose 1.2 percent to 1.28 billion marks. The group workforce is expected to increase this year to 28,000 thanks to the takeovers.
Investments last year totalled 146 million marks, down 20 million marks on the previous year.
($ = 1.686 German Marks) -- Douglas Busvine, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097 150
